item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows six triangles meeting at centre $O$.

Which claim explains why these triangles form a regular hexagon?

options.A: Six congruent equilateral triangles fit around $O$ because six $60^{\circ}$ angles sum to $360^{\circ}$, so the outer boundary has equal sides and equal $120^{\circ}$ angles.
options.B: Call the answer regular hexagon, and stop with no angle sum at $O$.
options.C: Any six triangles around $O$ form a regular hexagon, even when the triangles are not congruent and not equilateral.
options.D: The same assembly also builds a regular pentagon from five such triangles around $O$.
